question.problem:
Given that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{10}$ are I.I.D random variables, where

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(\frac{5}{2},{1}^{2}),\,1\le i\le 10,
$$

what is the distribution of $Y={X}_{1}+{X}_{2}+⋯+{X}_{10}?$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed (I.I.D) normal random variables, where 

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),\,1\le i\le n,
$$

then 

$$
Y={X}_{1}+{X}_{2}+⋯+{X}_{n}∼N(n\mu ,\,n{\sigma }^{2}).
$$

Therefore, since ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{10}$ are mutually independent, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}Y={X}_{1}+{X}_{2}+⋯+{X}_{10} & ∼N(10\cdot \frac{5}{2},\,10\cdot {1}^{2}) \\  & ∼N(10\cdot \frac{5}{2},\,10\cdot 1) \\  & =N(25,10).\end{aligned}
$$
